blocks.text: Why Slack is essential for community builders on Mac

Community builders rely on Slack to bridge the gap between team members and their community. On macOS, the desktop app provides a dedicated space for this work. You can keep it separate from your browser. This helps you focus when you need to switch between community moderation and internal team planning.

Speed is your best friend when managing multiple channels. Every second you save on navigation adds up during a long day of community management. Use Command + / to open the cheat sheet inside the app. This shows you every shortcut available for your current workspace.

items: Command + K: Use the quick switcher to jump between channels or DMs.
Command + G: Open general search to find past conversations.
Command + ,: Open your preferences to adjust notification settings.
Shift + Enter: Create a line break in your message without sending it.
Command + B: Bold your text to highlight important community announcements.

blocks.text: Community builders often face a flood of notifications. If you feel overwhelmed, use the Threads view to keep discussions contained. You can reply in a thread to keep the main channel clear for announcements. This practice helps members find information later without scrolling through dozens of irrelevant messages.
If Slack starts to lag on your Mac, use Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This is the most common fix for performance issues.
blocks.title: Fixing slow performance

blocks.text: Community management is an always on role, but you need time for deep work. Set your status to let members know when you are busy. You can use the Slack status feature to indicate if you are in a meeting or focusing on a project. This sets clear expectations for response times.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you manage your workspace. When you are inside Slack, hold Option + Command to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur can point to the search bar or guide you through creating a new channel. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your focus on the community.

Many community builders struggle with context switching. You might be in a Slack channel, then jump to a browser to update a member record. Keep your Slack app updated to version 4.53.x or later to ensure you have the latest performance improvements. Slack updates its requirements twice a year, so checking for updates ensures you stay secure on macOS.

blocks.text: Slack is a powerful tool when used correctly. By mastering the keyboard shortcuts and using tools like Lazur to manage your tasks, you can reduce the time spent on administrative chores. This leaves you with more time to focus on what matters most: your community members.

faq.question: How do I find old messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Use the search bar with Command + G. Use modifiers like from:name or in:channel to narrow down your results.

faq.question: Does Slack for Mac require a specific version of macOS?
faq.answer: Yes, Slack currently requires macOS 14 Sonoma or above for the latest versions.

faq.question: How can Lazur help me in Slack?
faq.answer: Lazur can answer questions about your screen, point out buttons you cannot find, or guide you through complex settings when you hold Option + Command.

faq.question: What is the best way to keep Slack clean?
faq.answer: Use threads for replies, mute channels that are not urgent, and use the Threads view to track ongoing conversations.
